evals.prompt: Je veux créer une page de contenu sur le portail v2 de démonstration (id d5902565-a54d-4981-99cd-42534bd6c793) qui présente un cas d'usage, avec un titre, une intro, un diagramme Mermaid et la carte STAR embarquée. Je suis dans le navigateur via Playwright, connecté sur koumoul.com. Comment tu t'y prends ?
evals.expected_output: Should use the manager API in same-origin fetch from the koumoul.com origin (not from the portal subdomain), and the 3-step flow: POST /portals-manager/api/pages (type generic, owner account with type/id/name — name is mandatory, otherwise 400 with empty body —, minimal config), PATCH /pages/:id with { draftConfig, portals }, POST /pages/:id/draft to publish. Should mention checking permissions first (publishing to the demo portal requires admin on its owner Koumoul/marketing; the current user may only be admin of another department) and using the public GET /portals-manager/api/portals/:id/public to confirm the portal identity/URL. Should mention slug (genericMetadata.slug or auto-generated from title) and the URL /pages/<slug>.

evals.prompt: Mon diagramme Mermaid s'affiche tout petit et illisible dans la page du portail. Le SVG a un viewBox de 1869 et fait 668 px de large à l'écran. Comment je le rends lisible ?
evals.expected_output: Should explain that the mermaid block inserts the SVG with width:100% capped at the natural width, so a wide diagram (typically flowchart LR with many parallel columns) is scaled down to ~0.36 and its font with it. Fixes: switch to flowchart TB, shorten node labels (one node width follows its text), aim for a natural width <= ~750 px so scale >= ~0.9 and effective font >= 11 px, keep fontSize 16px (raising it scales the viewBox proportionally and gains nothing), prefer linking to subgraph ids instead of every inner node. Should also mention the base theme's yellow/orange cluster fills and the %%{init: ...}%% directive with themeVariables (primaryColor/secondaryColor/clusterBkg white, clusterBorder grey) to neutralize them.

evals.prompt: Je veux intégrer la carte STAR qui est sur demo.koumoul.com dans une page d'un portail servi par koumoul.com (instance DataFair koumoul.com). Quel bloc utiliser et que faut-il configurer ?
evals.expected_output: Should distinguish the two blocks: application (same DataFair instance as the portal, resolves /data-fair/api/v1/applications/<id> and /data-fair/app/<slug>?d-frame=true, no CSP setup, displayMode/height and actionButtons) vs iframe (external URL, requires the domain in the portal config allowedFrameSources, otherwise the frame-src CSP blocks it; no height field). Here the app lives on another instance than the portal host, so use the iframe block with the app exposedUrl and add https://demo.koumoul.com to allowedFrameSources via PATCH /portals-manager/api/portals/:id {draftConfig} then POST /portals/:id/draft. Should mention verifying the app is public and testing in an anonymous browser context.

evals.prompt: J'ai créé la page dans le département test du portail v2, comme demandé, et maintenant je veux la publier sur le portail de démonstration qui appartient au département marketing de la même organisation. Que faut-il faire ?
evals.expected_output: Should explain that publishing on a portal requires admin on the portal's owner (Koumoul/marketing), not just on the page owner (test): either get admin on the marketing department/portal, or have the department listed in the portal's contributorDepartments so a contrib can request publication (requestedPortals) and a portal admin validates it. Moving = PATCH /pages/:id with the new portals array (remove old id, add target id) then POST /pages/:id/draft. Should mention that a department is a distinct account (org:test vs org:marketing), that an organization-level role covers all departments, and that after a role change in Simple Directory the browser session JWT must be refreshed by reloading a page on the host.

evals.prompt: Je veux la même page, avec le diagramme Mermaid, sur koumoul.com (le site commercial actuel à la racine). Tu peux la créer directement ?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize that koumoul.com root is currently served by portals v1 (legacy Nuxt 2, no /portals-manager page model, no mermaid block; raw <iframe> was tolerated in v1 markdown), out of this skill's scope. Should not attempt the v1 page with the v2 API. Should propose the v2 route: create the page in a v2 portal (manager at /portals-manager, front on a dedicated domain) and/or, if the page must be on v1, render the Mermaid diagram upstream (mermaid-cli or mermaid.ink) and embed it as an image, using a raw iframe in a text block for embeds.

evals.prompt: Je dois illustrer une page de cours avec des captures du formulaire de configuration d'un connecteur, avec des numéros qui pointent les champs à remplir. Je suis dans le navigateur MCP Playwright. Comment tu produis ces captures ?
evals.expected_output: Should apply the screenshot convention (light theme, 1440 px wide viewport, no scrollbar, red rectangles + numbered square badges) via scripts/annotate.js loaded with browser_evaluate, then a single second browser_evaluate call doing ANNO.reset(), ANNO.mark(ANNO.field(...)/ANNO.sel(...), n) and return ANNO.commit(). Should state that a non-empty commit() result means do not capture and fix first (ghost target hidden in a stepper, touching rectangles → frame the parent block, badge too far → pass a container to commit). Should set the viewport height before annotating so every target fits, re-install the script after each navigation, capture with browser_take_screenshot, and re-read the PNG to check badges over icons, absurd numeric values and product noise.

evals.prompt: J'ai uploadé une capture 1440x520 dans la médiathèque de la page et posé un bloc image avec height: 300. Sur le portail l'image apparaît coupée sur les côtés, et sur mobile elle est cassée. Pourquoi ?
evals.expected_output: Should explain that height on a wide image crops it: the content column is ~896 px wide, so an image flatter than the imposed ratio is scaled up then cut; compute height ≈ 896 × (520/1440) ≈ 324 or, for very wide banners (ratio > ~2.5), use cover: true without height. Should explain the mobile breakage by image.mobileAlt: the portal loads <id>-mobile which only exists when the server produced a mobile variant (width > ~1536 px), so set mobileAlt: false. Should mention verifying naturalWidth > 0, no -mobile in src and the displayed ratio equal to naturalWidth/naturalHeight.

evals.prompt: Ma page de cours a bien config._toc rempli mais le sommaire ne s'affiche pas, et le fil d'Ariane ne remonte pas à la page de listing du groupe. J'ai ajouté toc: true dans la config de la page, sans effet.
evals.expected_output: Should say there is no page-level or portal-level toc option (the page-config schema has unevaluatedProperties: false; the API silently accepts an unknown key which stays inert) and that the table of contents is enabled title block by title block with anchor: { enabled: true, inToc: true } on each H2/H3 (never the H1); the server recomputes _toc (readOnly, never written by hand) on PATCH. For the breadcrumb, should point to the group's rootPage (a page slug, not an id) set with PATCH /portals-manager/api/groups/:id with title mandatory in the body, propagated to genericMetadata.group.rootPage of every page of the group.

evals.prompt: Je veux faire une belle page d'accueil pour le portail v2 de démonstration (accueil actuel à remplacer) : un hero, trois cartes qui présentent les parcours, une section sur fond coloré avec un diagramme Mermaid, et un appel à l'action. Comment tu composes la page ?
evals.expected_output: Should read the portal first (GET /portal/api/portal: config.header.show to know whether a H1 is already rendered, config.theme.colors to pick tokens, config.defaults for elevation/rounded/hover, breadcrumb position), then apply the two-pass method from references/design.md: state the audience and the single job of the page, lay out the section skeleton, and avoid the generic title+paragraphs+button template. Composition: banner with fullWidth true only at page root (background.color: primary and no explicit text color so on-primary applies), title h2/titleTag h1, image hero with banner+wideImage+cover+height+fetchPriority if relevant; responsive-grid columns 3 with align stretch and cards using contentAlign start, border, rounded, elevation, and a link if a hover effect is wanted (hover is inert without link); banner with pt/pb 8-12 for the Mermaid section; button with usePortalConfig true. Must respect the rendering facts: line.color mandatory whenever a title line is requested, no mb on title blocks, markdown headings avoided in favor of title blocks, one single H1, anchors on H2/H3 only. Must not promise custom CSS, fonts or hex colors (tokens only), and should finish with publishing then the visual review (desktop 1440 + mobile screenshots, dark theme check).

evals.prompt: J'ai publié une page de présentation sur le portail et elle fait très « template » : titre centré, trois cartes identiques, de longs paragraphes, aucun relief. Qu'est-ce que tu améliores et comment ?
evals.expected_output: Should diagnose against references/design.md rather than restyle blindly: too many equally weighted sections and identical cards, centered long paragraphs, missing section rhythm (blocks stuck together or huge gaps), possibly markdown headings used instead of title blocks, title lines without line.color, no single signature moment. Should propose a composition passe: choose one memorable element dictated by the content (hero banner, Mermaid diagram, embedded application, real listing), keep the rest quiet, group content into titled sections with anchors (H2/H3), use a responsive-grid only if the content really is a set of peer items and align stretch + contentAlign start so cards share height, set mb 6-8 between sections and mb 0 inside cards/grids, use theme tokens only (background color for alternation, no explicit color inside colored banners). Should keep the API workflow (GET page, modify draftConfig, PATCH, POST /draft) and verify the rendering in an anonymous context with desktop and mobile screenshots plus the dark theme, not only the API response.
